summary: Parkevtate Vosianc updates UnitedHealth (UNH) after its post-2025 cost fumble. Management underestimated the cost to serve customers in 2025, then exited expensive markets, sold a Florida health unit to private equity, and raised insurance prices — and results have come in better than expected. He revised his FCF estimates up ~$3B per year starting 2026, lifting intrinsic value to $518/share, implying ~39-40% upside over 12-18 months despite the rapid share-price recovery. Margins likely won't return to pre-2025 levels until 2027-28; the business is not very lucrative (peak operating margin was under 10% in 2020; ROIC 8% TTM vs 16% peak), though scale is enormous (~$450B TTM revenue). Forward P/E of 16.5 remains at the low end of its multi-year range. He frames this as a buy-the-dip story that worked: he reiterated BUY through 2025 and early 2026 at prices from ~$230 to ~$280, contrasting with dip-buys that kept falling (Trade Desk, Pinterest, Lululemon). Reiterated BUY today — there is still upside as operations keep improving. Key caveat: earnings variability has been high since the 2025 fumble, a repeat of the cost-estimation error is the bear case. Call: UNH — BUY (intrinsic value $518, ~40% stated upside).
